questions.stem: In triangles ABC and DEF: AB = DE = 5 cm, angle B = angle E = 48 degrees, BC = EF = 7 cm. Which congruence condition applies?
questions.explanation: Two sides and the included angle (the angle between those two sides) are equal: AB = DE, angle B = angle E (included), and BC = EF. This is SAS (Side-Angle-Side).

questions.stem: Two triangles have the same three angles (50 degrees, 60 degrees, 70 degrees) but different side lengths. What can you conclude?

options.text: The triangles are similar but not necessarily congruent
The triangles are neither similar nor congruent

questions.explanation: AAA (Angle-Angle-Angle) proves similarity, not congruence. Two triangles with the same angles can be different sizes, so they are similar but not necessarily congruent.

questions.stem: In right-angled triangles PQR and STU: angle Q = angle T = 90 degrees, PR = SU = 13 cm (hypotenuses), PQ = ST = 5 cm. What is the length QR?
questions.explanation: The triangles are congruent by RHS. By Pythagoras: QR = sqrt(13^2 - 5^2) = sqrt(169 - 25) = sqrt(144) = 12 cm.

questions.stem: ABCD is a quadrilateral where AB = CD and BC = DA. The diagonal AC is common to triangles ABC and CDA. Which congruence condition proves these triangles are congruent?
questions.explanation: AB = CD (given), BC = DA (given), and AC = CA (common side). All three sides are equal, so the condition is SSS.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a valid condition for proving two triangles are congruent?
questions.explanation: SSA (two sides and a non-included angle) is NOT a valid congruence condition because of the ambiguous case -- two different triangles can share the same two sides and non-included angle.
